answer_text:
**Procol Harum** were the first to sing "A Whiter Shade of Pale." It was issued as their debut record on **12 May 1967**.

**Gary Brooker**, the Procol Harum frontman, provided the soaring vocals on the band's 1967 proto-prog rock classic. The music was composed by Gary Brooker and Matthew Fisher, while the lyrics were written by Keith Reid.

The song features a countermelody loosely based on J. S. Bach's Orchestral Suite No. 3 in D Major, played by Fisher's Hammond organ.

An enthusiastic response from listeners of the pirate radio station Radio London prompted Deram Records to rush-release the single, and it was an instant worldwide success, reaching No. 1 on the UK Singles Chart for six weeks and the same spot in eleven countries.

It remains one of the few singles to have sold more than **10 million copies**.

In 1977, the song was named joint winner (along with Queen's "Bohemian Rhapsody") of "The Best British Pop Single 1952–1977" at the Brit Awards. The song was also inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1998 and into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2018.
